chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn Abdillah (may Allah spare him) both narrated to me from Abdillah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar, from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Abi al-Qasim, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Isḥaq ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Kharijah, who said:

A man asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while I was with him, saying: 'What is the reward for one who visits the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?' He (peace be upon him) replied: 'Verily, when al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was slain, the lands wept for him. So Allah appointed four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, to weep for him until the Day of Judgment. Whoever visits him, acknowledging his right, they will escort him until they bring him to his safe haven. And if he becomes ill, they will visit him morning and evening. And if he dies, they will attend his funeral and seek forgiveness for him until the Day of Judgment.'

key_terms.زَارَ: To visit (specifically for religious devotion, Ziyarah)
key_terms.شُعْثاً غُبْراً: Disheveled and covered with dust (describing the angels)

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and angelic honors for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* emphasizes the cosmological significance of Karbala, where the weeping of the earth and the appointed four thousand angels establish a perpetual spiritual link between the martyr and his devotees. It underscores the Shia concept of *Ma'rifah* (gnostic recognition) of Imam al-Husayn’s rights, promising that such visitors receive active angelic intercession—from healing the sick to seeking forgiveness until the Day of Judgment—mirroring the divine promise of honor for the martyrs.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 8. My father and Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh both narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from Ibrāhīm ibn Mahziyār, from his brother ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Abil Qāsim, from Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from Isḥāq ibn Ibrāhīm, from Hārūn ibn Khārijah, who said:

I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) when a man asked him, “What is the reward for those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” Imam (a.s.) replied: Verily when Ḥusain (a.s.) was assaulted, even the lands cried over him. Therefore, Allāh dedicated four thousand angels, who are disheveled and covered with dust, who cry over him (and will continue to do so) until the Day of Judgment. These angels accompany those who go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.), while knowing his rights, until they arrive at their safe haven. And if they become ill, the angels will visit them every morning and evening. And when they die, these angels will attend their funerals and seek forgiveness for them until the Day of Judgment.
